However, Stokes’ smart planning and effective execution from his bowlers turned the tide. Potts and Atkinson stood out picking up 4 and 3 wickets respectively, while Carse and Stokes, though expensive, chipped in with key breakthroughs. A concern for England was the runs conceded to the last two wickets, which could prove costly. Now, it is time for their batters to take center stage again and do what they have done in this series so far. Join us in a bit for England's replay.

New Zealand started strongly, with the openers surviving testing spells and adding 105 for the first wicket. Will Young fell after a solid start, while Tom Latham notched a half-century before departing. Kane Williamson and Rachin Ravindra attacked from the outset, setting the stage for a big total, but Williamson’s unlucky dismissal triggered a collapse from 185/3 to 212/6 as the middle order just threw their wickets away. Mitchell Santner’s fiery fifty and Southee’s brisk cameo, however, pushed the total past 300. Then Santner and William O'Rourke added some important runs for the last wicket to take them near that 350-run mark.

New Zealand have been bowled out for 347! It is more or less the average first innings Test score on this ground and both teams will be content with it. With the sun shining and the pitch getting baked, it should be good for batting and England will want to take full advantage of that. However, the Kiwis will know the conditions better and will want to challenge the English batters. The crowd here is expecting Tim Southee to show up one last time and his record here is fantastic and he could be a big threat to the visitors.

OUT! BOWLED! That exclusive last wicket finally does come for England right after the Drinks break. Fired fuller and on the off stump, nips in just that slight bit. Mitchell Santner could not get his bat down in time and the ball goes through to rattle the stumps. Santner looks up in disappointment but he has played a fine knock of 76 off 117 for his team.

The Seddon Park pitch is likely to offer bounce for the seamers, with some turn expected as the game progresses. New Zealand’s bowlers will look to strike early in England’s reply, while England’s batters will need to remain patient on a surface that could offer variable bounce and pace. An exciting day of Test cricket awaits!

England's bowling on Day 1 was sharp and disciplined. Matthew Potts and Brydon Carse made breakthroughs at key moments, with Potts impressing in particular. His spell included the vital dismissal of Kane Williamson ​​​​​​that started the collapse for the Kiwis. The English seamers maintained pressure throughout the day. England will aim to clean up New Zealand's last wicket quickly and then focus on navigating what promises to be a challenging start to their innings.

New Zealand's batting on Day 1 showed moments of promise, with Tom Latham and Will Young providing stability at the top. Despite the early partnerships, the innings lost momentum during the middle overs. Kane Williamson’s return to form was a highlight, but he fell to Matthew Potts after looking well set. Mitchell Santner’s counter-attacking knock and Tim Southee's late fireworks was crucial in helping New Zealand surpass 300. As the team regroups for Day 2, the lower order’s fight against England’s disciplined attack could prove vital in setting a competitive total.

Hello and welcome to Day 2 of the third Test between New Zealand and England at Seddon Park, Hamilton. Day 1 was eventful, with the Kiwis finishing at 315/9 after being asked to bat first. The first session was remarkable, as no wickets fell throughout the entire period. However, the middle order faltered, with Kane Williamson and Rachin Ravindra falling in quick succession. Mitchell Santner's quick-fire 50 was a bright spot, but England's bowlers, led by Matthew Potts and Brydon Carse, dominated the later stages of the day.

Right then, that is it from this action-packed Day 1 of the final Test. With just one wicket left, New Zealand will hope that Mitchell Santner can add as many runs as possible while England will want to wrap things up quickly. Day 2 will begin at 10 pm GMT, but you can join us early for all the build-up. Cheers!

England roared back in the final session, turning the game on its head with sharp bowling and smart tactics. Kane Williamson’s dismissal by Matthew Potts, albeit with some luck, triggered a Kiwi collapse from 185/3 to 212/6, as the middle order faltered under pressure. England’s bowlers - Potts, Brydon Carse, Gus Atkinson, and Ben Stokes - executed their plans brilliantly, forcing poor shot selections from the hosts. However, Mitchell Santner and Matt Henry steadied the ship with a gritty 41-run stand before Tim Southee’s fireworks, including three towering sixes, pushed New Zealand past 300. Santner capped off the day in style with a big hit to reach his fifty, setting up a thrilling Day 2!

In the second session, England struck back with key wickets, but New Zealand kept the scoreboard ticking, heading into Tea in a strong position. Will Young fell early after Lunch, while skipper Tom Latham crafted a classy 63 before being dismissed, despite Ben Duckett dropping him twice earlier. Kane Williamson brought flair with crisp boundaries, but a late strike from Brydon Carse removed Rachin Ravindra just before Tea, halting the hosts' momentum. Gus Atkinson and Matthew Potts toiled hard for breakthroughs, but England struggled to contain the runs.

New Zealand dominated the morning session of the final Test, racing to 93/0 in 28 overs after being sent into bat by Ben Stokes. Captain Tom Latham and Will Young, playing his first match of the series, batted with remarkable composure, leaving England’s bowlers frustrated. They left the good balls, punished the loose ones, and built a solid opening stand, setting a commanding tone. England’s bowlers struggled to find rhythm despite the pitch offering extra bounce, with edges falling short and luck favoring the visitors.

SESSION SUMMARY - 143 runs and 6 wickets in 30 overs! A gripping opening day of Test cricket comes to an end! The pendulum shifted both ways but at the moment, this game hangs in the balance. We saw New Zealand dominate at first, but then England fought back excellently to make a game out of this one. However, the Kiwis had the final say as they smashed 76 runs in the last 8 overs of the day. With both sides exchanging hard blows, we are surely in for some thrilling moments in this match.

... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

England stuck with the four seamers and did not turn to Shoaib Bashir's turn. It worked for them but they could not contain the runs. It was Gus Atkinson who got them the first breakthrough but they had to toil very hard after that until Matthew Potts strangled Tom Latham down the leg side. Ben Duckett was a relieved man as he dropped him twice once on 12 and then on 53, but both were difficult chances. Just as the hosts were taking control again, Brydon Carse got rid of the in-form Rachin Ravindra just before the end of the session. The visitors will look to make early inroads in the next session and test the Kiwi middle order. Join us at 3 am GMT to catch all the exciting action of the last session.

Will Young couldn’t add to his Lunch score, falling soon after New Zealand crossed the 100-run mark. However, skipper Tom Latham continued to lead the charge in his usual composed style. Kane Williamson came in next and injected momentum with a counter-attacking approach, hitting some crisp early boundaries. Latham brought up a fluent fifty but was dismissed for 63. Rachin Ravindra then joined Williamson, and the pair looked assured at the crease, combining solid defense with calculated aggression. But a loose shot from Ravindra cost him his wicket at the stroke of Tea giving the visitors an opening going into the last session.

SESSION SUMMARY - 79 runs and 3 wickets in 25 overs! Probably a shared session! England managed to pick up a few crucial wickets, but New Zealand kept the runs flowing at a steady pace. As the players head into the Tea break, the hosts find themselves in a strong position, setting the stage for an intriguing final session.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities! A big cheer from the crowd for Tim Southee as he walks off and it is the England players who are taking up their respective field positions. Tom Latham and Will Young are the two openers for New Zealand. Matthew Potts has the new red cherry in his hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

We are moments away from the start but before that, the man of the moment, Tim Southee, receives a guard of honor as this will be his last ever Test match. He is carrying his daughter onto the field and it is an emotional moment as the whole crowd is standing on their feet. Now, the players from both sides line up for their respective national anthems. It will be England's first followed by the national anthem of New Zealand.

Tim Southee is up for a quick chat. He says that any Test match you play for New Zealand is special. Adds Hamilton has been a ground where he played a lot of his cricket and wants to finish on a high and a perfect place to end his career. Mentions that he wants to end on a positive note. Adds that he has played a 100-odd Test matches and has made special friendships. Concludes by saying that he always enjoyed watching the game as a fan and looking forward to it.

PITCH REPORT - The pitch at Seddon Park looks brown with a tinge of green in there. There is a normal breeze flowing across the ground. It will get hotter as the days progress and will flatten out in the latter stages of the game and will become more and more conducive for spin.

Tom Latham, the New Zealand captain says that it looks like a decent surface and there is a lot of grass and he is happy to bat first as he wants to post a big score. Adds that there is an opportunity to do good in this final Test for the team and end off on a high. Informs that there are two changes in the team.

Ben Stokes, the skipper of England says that when the team came to the ground this morning, there wasn't a cloud in the sky but it seems there are some clouds looming around. Further mentions that Potts is added in the pace battery in place of Chris Woakes. Adds that they have played some really good cricket throughout the series but New Zealand never give up easily. Concludes by saying that they are going to go about their game the same way they have throughout the series.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Tom Latham (C), Will Young (In place of Devon Conway), Kane Williamson, Rachin Ravindra, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Blundell (WK), Glenn Phillips, Mitchell Santner (In place of Nathan Smith), Matt Henry, Tim Southee, William O'Rourke.

England (Playing XI) - Zak Crawley, Ben Duckett, Jacob Bethell, Joe Root, Harry Brook, Ollie Pope (WK), Ben Stokes (C), Gus Atkinson, Brydon Carse, Matthew Potts (In place of Chris Woakes), Shoaib Bashir.

Stay tuned as the teams battle for supremacy in what promises to be a gripping five days of cricket! The weather forecast predicts clear skies with temperatures hovering around 22 degrees, ideal for uninterrupted cricket. With both captains keen to make the right call at the toss, a hard pitch full of green grass suggests that batting first might not be the best approach, since early movement with the new ball could pose a challenge. Compared to day one, there are many more predictions of rain interruptions for day three. The action on Day 1 is not far away. Toss and team news in a bit.

England, under Ben Stokes’ dynamic leadership, continues to embrace its aggressive 'Bazball' philosophy, which has seen them dominate batting lineups and pile up runs at a brisk rate. Harry Brook’s sensational form, amassing more than 300 runs in the series, has been a key factor in England's batting strength. On the bowling front, Gus Atkinson and Brydon Carse have been standout performers, collectively claiming 24 wickets in the series. With Matthew Potts replacing Chris Woakes in the pace battery to bring in sheer pace, they will have an impeccable mixture of pace and control in the mix, as England’s attack remains a potent threat. They may consider Shoaib Bashir to exploit spin-friendly conditions later in the match as the grass dries out after being baked for the first two days.

Team news suggests a possible inclusion of Will Young to bolster the batting department as Devon Conway has been given time off for personal reasons. With the pitch expected to deteriorate as the game progresses, the hosts have a better track record at this venue, having not lost a Test since 2012, showing that this might be the perfect venue to secure a win in this series and provide senior statesman, Tim Southee with a winning send-off.

New Zealand enters the contest brimming with confidence after a gritty fightback in the second Test, as the danger of losing the series 3-0 hangs over them. Kane Williamson still remains the backbone of their batting lineup, given his track record at home and being amongst the most technically sound batters in the lineup, averaging 94.26 at the ground, with six hundreds, including a career-best 251 against the West Indies. The Kiwis also rely heavily on pacers William O'Rourke and Matt Henry, who have taken crucial wickets for the team at important moments in this series. Tim Southee’s record at Seddon Park has been stellar in recent appearances at the venue.

Although England have already taken the series in the second Test match, it is still expected to be an intense battle.
